jobs.title: Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning and Analysis will help lead the development of the MBTA’s five-year capital plan through data analysis, engagement with internal and external stakeholders, and the development of decision-support tools. Working with MBTA executive leadership, the Deputy Chief of Capital Strategy, and the Senior Director of Capital Program Planning, the Deputy Director of Capital Program Planning will help create a fiscally constrained five-year capital plan that will translate the vision and goals set by the Governor, Secretary, MBTA Board of Directors, and General Manager into an achievable portfolio of tangible capital programs and projects.

The Deputy Director, working with other members of the Capital Program Planning team, will develop, implement, and monitor the process of developing the MBTA’s five-year Capital Investment Plan (CIP). The Deputy Director will also oversee processes related to project implementation, including processing project funding changes and performing ongoing analyses of capital project performance. In partnership with stakeholders across the Massachusetts Department of Transportation (MassDOT) and MBTA organizations, including Deputy Chiefs, Directors, and Project Managers, the Deputy Director will be responsible for conducting quantitative analyses and developing related insights for internal decision-making and public presentations or communication related to the capital program.

Duties & Responsibilities

Lead the development of the MBTA’s $10.3B five-year Capital Investment Plan (CIP) in close collaboration with the Capital Program Planning Team, MBTA Chiefs and Deputy Chiefs, Operations leadership, asset owners, project directors and managers, and individuals at other State agencies such as MassDOT and the Executive Office of Administration and Finance.
Manage conversations in a high-pressure environment with agency leadership, municipal elected and local officials, federal partners in United States Department of Transportation (USDOT), Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), state partners, and staff at the various municipal planning agencies through which federal funding is allocated.
Develop and manage processes for identifying, reviewing, evaluating, and prioritizing potential capital projects for funding as part of the annual CIP update.
Engage with MBTA subject matter experts, including the Asset Management, Safety, Environmental, Security, and Systemwide Accessibility departments, to evaluate capital project requests.
Create and oversee processes to assist with implementation of the Capital Program throughout the fiscal year. Proactively identify project budget risks and monitor capital project performance to address funding needs that arise in-between annual updates to the capital plan. Manage capital funding changes between annual CIP updates to ensure alignment with approved project budget estimates at completion, schedules, performance measures, and other milestones in close collaboration with the Capital Finance and Accounting and Project Controls departments.
Evaluate and improve upon recent process to conduct project reviews for all projects over $15M each year with agency leadership. Goal of these reviews is to ensure that projects are aligned with agency priorities and are managed well to result in on-budget outcomes. Develop strategies to bring more attention to projects that are not progressing or are not the best use of funds in a highlight constrained environment.
Working with the Senior Director of CIP Development, create a data governance and management strategy for the CIP Development team, ensuring that capital project datasets are maintained and updated to allow for ongoing analysis.
Utilize data visualization, business intelligence, and geospatial intelligence systems (GIS) tools to collect, display, and analyze project data, contributing to informed decision-making within the capital program.
Design and develop executive- and public-facing presentations, reports, and other communication materials related to the MBTA's capital program, including the annual CIP book and associated web content, which will be shared with a variety of stakeholders, including the MBTA Board of Directors, the Boston Region Metropolitan Planning Organization, the MBTA Advisory Board, and members of the general public.
Develop and implement a public outreach strategy for the annual update to the CIP in coordination with External Affairs, Public Engagement, Customer Experience, and other MBTA departments.
Oversee the management of capital project portfolios by Senior Analysts, ensuring that important project information is communicated to Capital Program Planning leadership. Engage with staff from Commonwealth, Federal, and municipal partners to ensure compliance with their processes and procedures and explore funding opportunities.
Identify and implement improvements to funding-related processes to maximize the impact of capital investment and ensure the efficient utilization of funds.
Support the development of the Capital Program Planning Department, including hiring, training, and managing staff as appropriate.
Perform all other duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location specific functions.

Supervision

Directly supervise one or more Senior Analysts.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Public Administration, Business Administration, Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Economics, or a related field.
Five (5) years of relevant experience in a budgeting, planning, quantitative, and/or research role.
Two (2) years of supervisory, managerial, and/or leadership experience.
Effective organizational, analytical, writing, multi-tasking, and time management skills.
Advanced skill in MS Office, including Excel and PowerPoint.
Ability to organize data, communicate insights and conclusions, and exercise effective problem-solving skills.
Ability to work in a collaborative and team-oriented manner.
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information in an appropriate manner.
Excellent communication, analytical, and presentation skills with the ability to obtain buy-in with key stakeholders at all levels of the organization and influence their decision-making.
Highly organized with the ability to manage time, resources, and people, handling multiple programs simultaneously.
Demonstrated data analysis skills, including the ability to conduct program analysis and identify key performance indicators.
Ability to learn quickly, take direction, work independently, and use creative, collaborative, and consultative approaches to resolve issues.

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate degree from an accredited institution with an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitute for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

Master’s degree from an accredited institution in Public Administration, Business Administration, Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Economics, or a related field.
Experience in planning, budgeting, data analysis, or capital project management in a public agency or within the transportation industry.
Experience working with Federal and State transportation funding, include knowledge of applicable regulations
Experience with data visualization, business intelligence, and/or geospatial information system (GIS) tools and software programs.
Knowledge of Trimble Unity Connect Project Management Information System.

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
Intern / co-op staff must be enrolled full or part-time in an accredited educational program and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 for the entire duration of the internship / co-op. Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.

Disclaimers And Definitions

General Disclaimer: The statements contained in this job description are intended to describe a summary, general nature, and complexity of typical job functions and do not represent an exhaustive list of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities required of staff assigned to this position.
Application Completion: It is each applicant’s responsibility to ensure application details are entered completely and correctly, including updated work and education histories (past and current). Incomplete applications may not be considered. Attachments do not substitute for application fields. The recruitment team does not have access to existing employee data / history.
Application Deadlines: Applicants should apply as soon as possible, as the MBTA may stop considering applicants after a sufficiently large applicant pool is established.

jobs.title: Regional Director Of Operations
jobs.description:
Regional Director of Operations

Our Culture:

We are a highly entrepreneurial company limited only by our imagination. Diversity and teamwork are major aspects of our culture. Our property associates are a highly team-focused group bringing out the uniqueness of each associate to provide great products and services. Success comes to those who continuously seek opportunities to learn and pass on new knowledge. We always strive to be better, never bored, and never complacent. Our teams thrive on hard work, inclusivity, and producing outstanding experiences. We endeavor to make our fellow associates feel comfortable and entrepreneurial so that they can engage unhindered. Finally, giving back to the community is also vital to our culture. Our properties live by the philosophy that they are an important part of their communities and look for ways to partner in the local community to make a difference.

Job Description:

The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for overall operational excellence for the properties in their area and will be a leader who exemplifies and embodies our Culture. This role will support all disciplines to deliver outstanding results, lead strategic initiatives, drive associate development, and work with the team to maximize revenues and grow profit across our portfolio. This leader will work with a remarkable group of associates who insist you are highly communicative, dedicated, balanced, and collaborative. The person in this position must be able to roll their sleeves up and assist our teams when needed, living our “ONE TEAM. ONE VISION.” philosophy. This person must also provide innovative strategic strategies that align with our mission to be the best, most respected hotel company in America.

The job is simple:

Focus on ways to promote and engage in internal growth programs.

Continuously exemplify and live by our Culture.

Meet/exceed our company goals and three metrics.

Job Requirements:

Work jointly with other company leaders to ensure that key objectives are met.
Work with all senior leaders to ensure we are leading in associate engagement and loyalty, produce top brand performance in guest satisfaction, deliver accurate forecasts that meet and exceed financial performance.
Have oversight of and mentor highly engaged and top-performing area General Managers to support Associates, Sales, Revenue, Engineering, Food & Beverage, and Operations.
Coach and mentor all leaders to help them reach their full potential; establish clear expectations in their role.
Regularly hold and actively participate in meetings with the properties' Leadership teams to review performance and analyze data and industry trends to improve processes and procedures.
Work with leadership on property capital improvements and budget oversite.
Conduct monthly property visits to review all aspects of the operation and serve as a cultural ambassador of our core values to all associates.
Work closely with sales & marketing and revenue management to help achieve and exceed RevPAR goals.
Work with all areas of the leadership teams taking time to understand our programs and how programs or practices affect our operations and culture; be the catalyst to prevent any working silos.
Be transparent with all stakeholders, taking the time to understand everyone's responsibilities and how to best partner with the individuals to determine field subject matter experts, celebrate our culture, and seek feedback while holding everyone accountable.
Establish regular communication with the field teams to understand their needs, support property initiatives and ensure we are the community's living room.

Necessary Skills:

Has the highest degree of integrity and is humble, living by the Golden Rule
Approachable and easily engage in general conversation to build rapport quickly, outstanding interpersonal skills for a wide range of audiences
Must have exceptional organization, follow-through, and excellent communication skills.
Must have a proven record of the ability to lead others at all levels of the operations, develop leaders and teams successfully, hold everyone accountable, and produce a unified team
Demonstrated success in owner relations within a variety of situations and a track record in achieving results
Minimum of three (3) years in a Multi-Property operational oversight role within upper midscale, lifestyle, or luxury hospitality companies- preferred
Willingness to travel +/- 80% of the time or when needed; travel will ebb and flow with the needs of the business.
Approaches all items with a collaborative effort; values input, and experiences of others look to uncover all areas that need to be addressed to remove any barriers.
Passionate for best-in-class results; comfortable in being “the” decision maker when needed yet can “allow” others to take the lead when needed.
Prioritizes and organizes work, being adaptable and flexible to accommodate when needed
Has a track record of maintaining confidentiality and knows how to use discretion when appropriate; understands the difference between transparency and confidentiality
Able to work with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds
Values of dedication, innovation, showing respect, being driven by excellence, being community-focused, and having a spirit of service.

Vision Hospitality Group is an equal opportunity/AA/Disability/Veteran employer. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, Vision Hospitality Group celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment and a sense of belonging for all associates. We do not discriminate and believe everybody should be proud of who they are, represent their culture and heritage, and live by the Golden Rule.

Vision Hospitality Group LLC, offers the following benefits:

Paid Time Off
Optional Health, Wellness and Care benefits
Health Reimbursement Program
Flexible Spending Account
Stay Discounts
Optional Company paid Life Insurance
401(k) and 401(k) matching
Employee Assistance Program
Several Voluntary and Supplemental Insurance Options
Select Paid Holidays and One Personal Floating Holiday
Loyalty Incentives and Other Unique Incentive Programs

Not Applicable

Employment type

Full-time

Job function

Management and Manufacturing

jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
About Acclime

Acclime is a premier corporate and advisory services provider helping companies seamlessly expand and operate across Asia-Pacific. We employ over 2,000 professionals across the region, delivering a comprehensive suite of services spanning corporate governance, accounting, tax, trade and HR, payroll and compliance, fund administration and a wide range of advisory services. Our mission is to guide international businesses through complex regulatory environments, enabling them to establish, scale and succeed in Asia.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Business Development Director based in the East Coast or the Midwest. This role will drive outbound business development from the US into North Asia (with a primary focus on China, Hong Kong, Korea and Japan) and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

The ideal candidate will have lived and worked in North Asia and bring a deep understanding of the business culture, networks and market dynamics in the region. The role reports directly to the Group Commercial Director and the Commercial Director North Asia.

Key Responsibilities:

Partnership development:
Build and nurture strategic partnerships with intermediaries such as law firms, accounting firms and other professional advisors.
Lead generation:
Leverage personal networks, industry conferences and events to generate new business opportunities.
Client acquisition:
Identify and engage US-based companies seeking to expand into China and Asia or scale existing operations.
Brand building:
Actively promote Acclime’s brand in the US market through thought leadership, networking and visibility at key industry events.
Market expertise:
Provide insights into regulatory, cultural and operational challenges for clients entering North Asia markets.
Revenue growth:
Drive measurable business outcomes through proactive outreach and relationship management.

Key Requirements:

Proven track record in business development, preferably in professional services or consulting. Candidates with a legal or accounting background preferred.
Must have lived in North Asia (China, Hong Kong, Korea or Japan) with strong regional networks.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills with US-based corporates and intermediaries.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

Here's what makes this role a winner:

Opportunity to work with a dynamic, international team and play a pivotal role in Acclime’s growth across Asia-Pacific.
Own and drive strategic revenue growth initiatives and shape business direction.
Attractive commission scheme tied to performance.
Access to a broad range of client portfolio across industries.
Medical coverage and retirement savings plan with employer contributions.

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Job function

Business Development and General Business

Industries

Business Consulting and Services

jobs.title: Executive Director of Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Job Title
Executive Director of Technology Operations

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment

Partner with product management, engineering, IT, finance, HR, and business leaders to align technology operations with business priorities.
Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives and technology-enabled business growth.
Ensure effective coordination across global technology teams.

VIII. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead high-performing technology operations teams.
Develop leadership capabilities, succession planning, and talent development programs.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Promote employee engagement and collaboration across technology functions.

Qualifications
Education Background

Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related fields.
Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

Work Experience

Typically 18+ years of experience in technology operations, IT management, engineering operations, or related functions, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles.
Proven experience managing large-scale technology organizations, digital transformation programs, and enterprise operations.
Strong background in software development operations, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and technology governance.
Experience in multinational corporations or high-growth technology-driven organizations preferred.

Show more

Show less

Seniority level

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Job function

Information Technology

Industries

Education

new_jobs.title: Regional Director Of Operations
new_jobs.description:
Regional Director of Operations

Our Culture:

We are a highly entrepreneurial company limited only by our imagination. Diversity and teamwork are major aspects of our culture. Our property associates are a highly team-focused group bringing out the uniqueness of each associate to provide great products and services. Success comes to those who continuously seek opportunities to learn and pass on new knowledge. We always strive to be better, never bored, and never complacent. Our teams thrive on hard work, inclusivity, and producing outstanding experiences. We endeavor to make our fellow associates feel comfortable and entrepreneurial so that they can engage unhindered. Finally, giving back to the community is also vital to our culture. Our properties live by the philosophy that they are an important part of their communities and look for ways to partner in the local community to make a difference.

Job Description:

The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for overall operational excellence for the properties in their area and will be a leader who exemplifies and embodies our Culture. This role will support all disciplines to deliver outstanding results, lead strategic initiatives, drive associate development, and work with the team to maximize revenues and grow profit across our portfolio. This leader will work with a remarkable group of associates who insist you are highly communicative, dedicated, balanced, and collaborative. The person in this position must be able to roll their sleeves up and assist our teams when needed, living our “ONE TEAM. ONE VISION.” philosophy. This person must also provide innovative strategic strategies that align with our mission to be the best, most respected hotel company in America.

The job is simple:

Focus on ways to promote and engage in internal growth programs.

Continuously exemplify and live by our Culture.

Meet/exceed our company goals and three metrics.

Job Requirements:

Work jointly with other company leaders to ensure that key objectives are met.
Work with all senior leaders to ensure we are leading in associate engagement and loyalty, produce top brand performance in guest satisfaction, deliver accurate forecasts that meet and exceed financial performance.
Have oversight of and mentor highly engaged and top-performing area General Managers to support Associates, Sales, Revenue, Engineering, Food & Beverage, and Operations.
Coach and mentor all leaders to help them reach their full potential; establish clear expectations in their role.
Regularly hold and actively participate in meetings with the properties' Leadership teams to review performance and analyze data and industry trends to improve processes and procedures.
Work with leadership on property capital improvements and budget oversite.
Conduct monthly property visits to review all aspects of the operation and serve as a cultural ambassador of our core values to all associates.
Work closely with sales & marketing and revenue management to help achieve and exceed RevPAR goals.
Work with all areas of the leadership teams taking time to understand our programs and how programs or practices affect our operations and culture; be the catalyst to prevent any working silos.
Be transparent with all stakeholders, taking the time to understand everyone's responsibilities and how to best partner with the individuals to determine field subject matter experts, celebrate our culture, and seek feedback while holding everyone accountable.
Establish regular communication with the field teams to understand their needs, support property initiatives and ensure we are the community's living room.

Necessary Skills:

Has the highest degree of integrity and is humble, living by the Golden Rule
Approachable and easily engage in general conversation to build rapport quickly, outstanding interpersonal skills for a wide range of audiences
Must have exceptional organization, follow-through, and excellent communication skills.
Must have a proven record of the ability to lead others at all levels of the operations, develop leaders and teams successfully, hold everyone accountable, and produce a unified team
Demonstrated success in owner relations within a variety of situations and a track record in achieving results
Minimum of three (3) years in a Multi-Property operational oversight role within upper midscale, lifestyle, or luxury hospitality companies- preferred
Willingness to travel +/- 80% of the time or when needed; travel will ebb and flow with the needs of the business.
Approaches all items with a collaborative effort; values input, and experiences of others look to uncover all areas that need to be addressed to remove any barriers.
Passionate for best-in-class results; comfortable in being “the” decision maker when needed yet can “allow” others to take the lead when needed.
Prioritizes and organizes work, being adaptable and flexible to accommodate when needed
Has a track record of maintaining confidentiality and knows how to use discretion when appropriate; understands the difference between transparency and confidentiality
Able to work with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds
Values of dedication, innovation, showing respect, being driven by excellence, being community-focused, and having a spirit of service.

Vision Hospitality Group is an equal opportunity/AA/Disability/Veteran employer. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, Vision Hospitality Group celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment and a sense of belonging for all associates. We do not discriminate and believe everybody should be proud of who they are, represent their culture and heritage, and live by the Golden Rule.

Paid Time Off
Optional Health, Wellness and Care benefits
Health Reimbursement Program
Flexible Spending Account
Stay Discounts
Optional Company paid Life Insurance
401(k) and 401(k) matching
Employee Assistance Program
Several Voluntary and Supplemental Insurance Options
Select Paid Holidays and One Personal Floating Holiday
Loyalty Incentives and Other Unique Incentive Programs

new_jobs.title: Business Development Director
new_jobs.description:
About Acclime

Acclime is a premier corporate and advisory services provider helping companies seamlessly expand and operate across Asia-Pacific. We employ over 2,000 professionals across the region, delivering a comprehensive suite of services spanning corporate governance, accounting, tax, trade and HR, payroll and compliance, fund administration and a wide range of advisory services. Our mission is to guide international businesses through complex regulatory environments, enabling them to establish, scale and succeed in Asia.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Business Development Director based in the East Coast or the Midwest. This role will drive outbound business development from the US into North Asia (with a primary focus on China, Hong Kong, Korea and Japan) and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

The ideal candidate will have lived and worked in North Asia and bring a deep understanding of the business culture, networks and market dynamics in the region. The role reports directly to the Group Commercial Director and the Commercial Director North Asia.

Key Responsibilities:

Partnership development:
Build and nurture strategic partnerships with intermediaries such as law firms, accounting firms and other professional advisors.
Lead generation:
Leverage personal networks, industry conferences and events to generate new business opportunities.
Client acquisition:
Identify and engage US-based companies seeking to expand into China and Asia or scale existing operations.
Brand building:
Actively promote Acclime’s brand in the US market through thought leadership, networking and visibility at key industry events.
Market expertise:
Provide insights into regulatory, cultural and operational challenges for clients entering North Asia markets.
Revenue growth:
Drive measurable business outcomes through proactive outreach and relationship management.

Key Requirements:

Proven track record in business development, preferably in professional services or consulting. Candidates with a legal or accounting background preferred.
Must have lived in North Asia (China, Hong Kong, Korea or Japan) with strong regional networks.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills with US-based corporates and intermediaries.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

Here's what makes this role a winner:

Opportunity to work with a dynamic, international team and play a pivotal role in Acclime’s growth across Asia-Pacific.
Own and drive strategic revenue growth initiatives and shape business direction.
Attractive commission scheme tied to performance.
Access to a broad range of client portfolio across industries.
Medical coverage and retirement savings plan with employer contributions.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director of Technology Operations
new_jobs.description:
Job Title
Executive Director of Technology Operations

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment

Partner with product management, engineering, IT, finance, HR, and business leaders to align technology operations with business priorities.
Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives and technology-enabled business growth.
Ensure effective coordination across global technology teams.

VIII. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead high-performing technology operations teams.
Develop leadership capabilities, succession planning, and talent development programs.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Promote employee engagement and collaboration across technology functions.

Qualifications
Education Background

Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related fields.
Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

Work Experience

Typically 18+ years of experience in technology operations, IT management, engineering operations, or related functions, including 8+ years in senior leadership roles.
Proven experience managing large-scale technology organizations, digital transformation programs, and enterprise operations.
Strong background in software development operations, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and technology governance.
Experience in multinational corporations or high-growth technology-driven organizations preferred.

Show more

Show less

Seniority level

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Job function

Information Technology

Industries

Education
